-122.08200,37.36830.name: Nova In Vitro Fertilization
-122.08200,37.36830.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Richard J. Schmidt, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-122.80378,45.48717.name: Oregon National Primate Research Center
-122.80378,45.48717.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Oregon Health and Science University. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-79.66827,44.41223.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, February 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

140.12100,36.02400.name: RIKEN BioResource Research Centre
140.12100,36.02400.company: The Institute of Physical and Chemical Research (RIKEN)
140.12100,36.02400.desc: A BSL4 laboratory, operational. Run by The Institute of Physical and Chemical Research (RIKEN). It is categorised as a private laboratory, working on human health. Containment space: 164 SqM. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

4.47000,52.16500.name: Biomedical Primate Research Centre
4.47000,52.16500.desc: The Dutch national primate centre, which has been under government pressure to reduce and eventually end primate research and has published reduction targets. A state-funded facility being wound down on political instruction is a different mechanism from any regulator refusing a licence.

-86.81000,33.51800.name: Society for Reproductive Endocrinology and Infertility
-86.81000,33.51800.desc: The US subspecialty body for fertility medicine, setting practice guidance in a field where almost nothing is set by statute. Embryo screening, the number transferred, donor limits and what may be offered as an add-on are all governed by professional consensus rather than law, which means the profession regulates itself and publishes its own outcome data.

-77.02700,38.99500.name: ARPA-H
-77.02700,38.99500.state: Washington DC — Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health
-77.02700,38.99500.desc: A US health research agency created in 2022 on the DARPA model, funding high-risk biomedical programmes on fixed timelines. Agencies built this way choose directions rather than reviewing proposals, which concentrates a great deal of influence over what gets attempted in a small number of programme managers.

-77.02700,38.99500.name: International Experts Group of Biosafety and Biosecurity Regulators
-77.02700,38.99500.state: Bethesda, Maryland — rotating chair, US secretariat
-77.02700,38.99500.desc: National regulators from eleven countries sharing practice on biosafety and biosecurity. Eleven is the number worth noticing: there are 27 countries with BSL4 laboratories, so most of the states running maximum containment are not in the room where regulators compare notes.

6.14010,46.23250.name: WHO Joint External Evaluation
6.14010,46.23250.desc: A voluntary peer review of a country's capacity to prevent, detect and respond to health emergencies, covering nineteen technical areas of which biosafety and biosecurity is one. Voluntary and public: a country choosing to be evaluated and publishing the result is the closest thing to an inspection that exists for laboratory biosafety anywhere.
